101.text: A canvas with id #app exists and is the render target
Spider has a body of at least 2 distinct primitives (e.g. abdomen and head)
Exactly 8 legs, each with at least 2 jointed segments (16+ leg parts), found in source or scene
Legs are driven by a per-frame time-based function (sinusoidal or equivalent), not a one-shot tween
Alternating diagonal gait: two leg groups with a half-period phase offset
Body bob is linked to the gait phase
Animation loops continuously with a period of roughly 1.5 to 2.5 seconds and no user input needed
A ground plane and at least one light exist; no external model assets are loaded
Page loads with no console errors

102.text: Single-page app boots with vite and renders to the canvas with id #app without console errors
Scene contains a ring-shaped portal frame and a platform or ground made of distinct geometry (not one flat quad)
The portal disc is a visibly animated surface (rotating or swirling pattern via shader, texture animation, or layered rotating meshes)
At least 100 particles orbit or spiral toward the portal and at least some rise and fade out
Portal emits colored light that falls on nearby geometry (a point light or equivalent) and its intensity pulses over time
Glow or bloom-like emphasis is applied to the portal and particles
Camera moves slowly (orbit or sway) or is user-orbitable, and ruined pillars or other surrounding props are present
window.__TASK_STATE__ is updated each frame with portalActive true, a particleCount above 100, and time that increases (probe)

103.text: index.html contains a canvas with id app, and the page is served by vite (vite dev or build output works)
The canvas fills the viewport and resizes on window resize (renderer size and camera aspect updated)
Canyon walls are built from multiple distinct rock masses or layered strata, not a single flat plane (source shows more than one wall mesh or a displaced or layered terrain)
A dusk sky is set up (gradient, sky model or background colour plus a low directional light with warm colour)
Distance fog or atmospheric haze is enabled and tinted to match the horizon colour
At least two kinds of ground clutter (for example boulders and shrubs) are placed, in multiple copies
The camera position is updated every frame along a path that loops (no hard jump visible, no user input required)
No uncaught errors or failed network requests at load (probe reports zero console errors)

104.text: Moving slab oscillates horizontally and is visible before any input
Space and canvas click/tap both drop the slab
Overlap trimming is implemented: the remaining slab width equals the overlap and the overhang becomes a falling piece
Perfect-drop tolerance keeps full width and awards a bonus
Total miss sets status to lost; 25 stacked slabs sets status won
R or click after game end restarts and resets score, height and status
DOM HUD outside the canvas shows score, session best and status
window.__TASK_STATE__ exposes status, score, height as specified

105.text: Page loads under vite with a canvas with id #app and no console errors on first load with zero plants.
A click on the canvas plants a new plant at the ground position under the cursor (ray or plane intersection, not a fixed position).
Plants grow over time from a small sprout to a larger mature form with a visibly different look, with growth running about 8 seconds, driven by elapsed time.
Each plant grows independently from its own plant time (later plants are smaller than earlier ones).
Appearance varies between plants (colour or size variation).
DOM overlay shows 'Plants: N' updating on every plant and on Clear, and the Clear button removes all plants.
window.__TASK_STATE__ exposes ready, plantCount and plants[{x,z,growth}] with growth in 0..1, and window.__plantAt(x,z) adds a plant.
Clicks that miss the ground are ignored, and 40+ plants render without obvious frame-rate collapse (instancing or reused geometry preferred).

106.text: Exactly three sphere meshes of equal radius are created and arranged in a row.
The glass sphere uses a transmissive/transparent material with an index of refraction or tint, not an opaque colour.
The metal sphere uses a metallic material with metalness near 1 and a low-to-mid roughness (anisotropy or streaked reflection is a bonus).
The fabric sphere uses a rough, non-metallic material with a procedural weave/noise texture, bump or normal map, and sheen or rim response.
An environment map or reflection source is configured and applied (procedurally generated, no network).
Key, fill and rim lights are authored, and shadows or contact shadows on the floor are enabled.
Floor is a curved/seamless backdrop or at least a floor plane with a light-grey material.
The key light position animates over time and window.__TASK_STATE__.keyLightX changes between frames.
Camera is fixed and frames all three spheres.
window.__EVAL_READY__ is set after the first frame.
